components.name: World Window Button
components.description: Colored CRT window tile used to select a project world. The tile fill and label color come from the world's accent token.
components.css: .ds-world-window { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 0.25rem; padding: 0; border: none; background: transparent; color: currentColor; cursor: pointer; outline: none; transition: transform 0.3s ease; } .ds-world-window:hover, .ds-world-window:focus-visible { transform: translateY(-4px) scale(1.02); } .ds-world-window:focus-visible { box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #ffffff; } .ds-world-window__tile { width: 3.5rem; height: 3.5rem; border: 1px solid hsla(0,0%,100%,0.25); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.05); transition: transform 0.15s ease; } .ds-world-window:hover .ds-world-window__tile, .ds-world-window:focus-visible .ds-world-window__tile { transform: translateY(-0.25rem); } .ds-world-window__label { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Nav Shelf
components.description: Floating pill jump-bar that appears after the hero scrolls out of view. Contains top/contact icons and world initial badges.
components.html: KAC
components.css: .ds-nav-shelf { position: fixed; bottom: 1.25rem; left: 50%; z-index: 50; transform: translateX(-50%); display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.25rem; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; background: #2d2844; border: 1px solid hsla(0,0%,100%,0.1); border-radius: 9999px; box-shadow: 0 10px 15px -3px rgba(0,0,0,0.1), 0 4px 6px -4px rgba(0,0,0,0.1); } .ds-nav-shelf__icon, .ds-nav-shelf__badge { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; color: #d4d4d4; text-decoration: none; border-radius: 9999px; transition: color 0.15s ease, background-color 0.15s ease; } .ds-nav-shelf__icon { padding: 0.5rem; } .ds-nav-shelf__icon:hover, .ds-nav-shelf__icon:focus-visible, .ds-nav-shelf__badge:hover, .ds-nav-shelf__badge:focus-visible { color: #f4a261; background: hsla(0,0%,100%,0.1); } .ds-nav-shelf__badge { width: 2.25rem; height: 2.25rem; font-family: 'Chakra Petch', sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-nav-shelf__svg { width: 1.25rem; height: 1.25rem; } .ds-nav-shelf__divider { width: 1px; height: 1rem; background: hsla(0,0%,100%,0.1); }

narrative.overview:
The site replaces the generic portfolio scroll with a single spatial scene: the visitor is inside a dim 90s bedroom, and a desk with a CRT monitor is the hub. The interface recedes so the artifact can lead; projects appear as colored windows open on the monitor, and navigation feels like a floating shelf above the desk. The mood is nostalgic, intimate, and quietly technical — a room built by someone who enjoys both craft and play.

The build commits to that scene literally: the hero is a full-viewport SVG room with an embedded HTML foreignObject for the interactive CRT windows. Light, texture, and material come from the room itself, not from abstract UI decorations.
keyCharacteristics: Full-viewport SVG scene as the homepage stage.
Warm desk-lamp light from the left and a cooler CRT phosphor glow from the monitor.
World colors are drawn from the room's existing light sources.
Uppercase display type with wide tracking for labels and the hero name.
Subtle scanlines, vignettes, and noise textures on the CRT and walls.
Reduced-motion fallbacks for all animated room effects.

rules.name: The One Lamp Rule
rules.body: Warm light always enters from the left; a hover-driven world tint is a brief color wash, not a second light source.

rules.name: The World-Color Rule
rules.body: Each world owns one accent already present in the room (Kitchen = lamp, Arcade = amber, Control = CRT). New worlds must derive their color from the existing palette.

rules.name: The Wide Tracking Rule
rules.body: Display text and labels stay uppercase with tracking no tighter than 0.04em; labels and mono UI text use 0.1em or wider. Tight tracking is out of character for this room.

rules.name: The Single Stage Rule
rules.body: The first viewport is one continuous room scene; do not break it into separate horizontal bands or card rows.

rules.name: The Light-First Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadows and lifts are secondary; the room's lamp and CRT glows do the real work of establishing depth.

rules.name: The Room Geometry Rule
rules.body: UI elements inside the scene are rounded; structural room elements (desk, walls, corkboard) are straight-edged.

dos: Do keep the first viewport as one continuous room scene with the CRT monitor as the hub.
Do derive every world accent from the existing palette (lamp, amber, CRT).
Do use uppercase labels with tracking of at least 0.1em for UI labels and at least 0.04em for display text.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: disable room-glow transitions and world-window hover lifts when reduced motion is requested.
Do hide the nav shelf while the hero is in view and slide it up only after scrolling.
donts: Don't add a kicker or eyebrow above the hero name; the heading carries its own weight.
Don't use gradient text for emphasis.
Don't drop a generic card grid into the first viewport.
Don't use blur or glass as a decorative surface treatment; the scene already has light, texture, and material.
Don't introduce a new accent color for a future world; map it to an existing light source in the room.
